_comment: Corpses and trophies (v0.61.0; user, design-progression.md stage 6b). A creature leaves its corpse where it dies (not one that bursts, like the lantern tick, and not a ghost). Picked up (g), the corpse is a trophy: hauled home whole, it takes pack slots by size. Butchered (b) it gives materials (the creature's drops in monsters.json; Harvesting helps). The trophymaster keeps the records: the heaviest of each creature, and the first of each quirk; a record pays (pay), anything else he turns away. The butcher breaks a trophy down into materials for nothing, more surely than you can in the field. kg: [usual weight, spread] (each one weighs usual x a normal roll around 1 with that spread, kept between low and high). slots: pack slots it takes. ALL NUMBERS, QUIRKS AND LINES ARE PLACEHOLDERS.

pay._comment: shards: a first record pays base[tier]; beating a record pays base[tier] x (1 + per_margin x the share it beat it by), at most most x base; a curiosity (the first of a quirk) pays curio x base.

scarred.name: scarred
scarred.note: Old wounds across its hide: it had won fights before yours.

pale.name: pale
pale.note: Pale all over, as if the colour had been drawn out of it.

old.name: old
old.note: Grey about the face and worn at the edges. It had lived a long time.

runt.name: runt
runt.note: Small for its kind, and all the fiercer for it.

misshapen.name: misshapen
misshapen.note: Something about it grew wrong: an extra ridge, a twisted limb.

first: Nobody's brought me a {creature} before. {weight}: that's the mark to beat now.
A {creature}! The wall's had a space for one of these. {weight}, and the record's yours.
record: New record! You brought in a {weight} {creature}. {extra}
big: How did you even haul this back?
My back hurts just looking at it.
You carried this all the way home?
small: That'll look well on the wall.
curio: A {quirk} {creature}! I've never had one of those. That goes up too.
Now that's something: a {quirk} {creature}. A first for the wall.
reject: {weight}? The record's {old}, {holder_s}. Not this one. The butcher might make use of it.
No, this won't do. {holder_s} {old} still stands. Try the butcher.
